shortName: NYU Grossman Long Island School of Medicine
additionalCoursework: The courses listed above are recommended only.  NYUGLISOM does not have specific pre-medical course requirements.  However, we place a high priority on evidence of applicants' academic readiness for successfully handling the rigor and fast pace of our three-year accelerated curriculum.  This includes strong, sustained academic achievement in introductory and upper level science courses -or- evidence of a clear upward trend in academic performance for those candidates who may have had a slow transition to college-level work.  Number of science credit hours taken per academic year is also evaluated to confirm an applicant's ability to successfully manage multiple, advanced science concepts/courses at the same time.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
NYU GLISOM's Office of Student Affairs supports individual and professional development initiatives that create a welcoming community for medical students. It's mission is to foster excellence, compassion, and integrity through proactive advising and career counseling for all students; and develop and implement programs, policies, and services that promote self-awareness, resilience, and well-being.  

Programing includes: 
- academic coaching
- career exploration and departmental advising
- student life
- wellness initiatives
- student groups and clubs
- para-curricular activities

Students have numerous opportunities to participate in clubs and activities, allowing them to explore areas of interest and collaborate with peers who share similar passion, and are encouraged to join existing clubs, organize new activities, and engage with our specialty interest groups. We also provide support for students to take on leadership roles, helping to enhance our student community.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Students volunteer in many community programs such as the WiSH free health clinic serving underinsured and uninsured individuals in the local area and the NYUGLISOM Envision Scholars Academy - a mentoring and advising program for local high school and college students interested in health careers.

In addition, our highly engaged student community has spearheaded many clubs, special interest groups, campus activities and community events. Among these include specialty interest groups in Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Obstetric & Gynecology, Family Medicine and General Surgery; Medical Ethics Society, Spanish or Mandarin Club; peer mentoring and tutoring; wellness representatives and class liaisons. 

For more information:
https://medli.nyu.edu/education/md-degree/md-student-resources/clubs-activities
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Located 17 miles east of New York City, the school is situated on Long Island in Nassau County in the suburban Village of Mineola easily accessible by car, train or bus and within walking distance to off-campus housing, shops, restaurants, and recreation.  

The school prioritizes a healthy school-life balance and encourages students to take advantage of the wide range of activities available in the local area such as 930-acre Eisenhower Park with hiking and biking trails, athletic fields, tennis courts and an Olympic-size aquatic center, Long Island's famous beaches, the UBS Arena with a seating capacity of over 18,000 that hosts professional indoor sporting events & headline concerts or Citi Field - home to the NY Mets.  Located directly across the street from the school, students can also take a 36-min train ride into New York City to see a Broadway show, visit the Statue of Liberty, bike ride around Central Park, visit some of the world's iconic museums or enjoy amazing food!
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
We provide below market-rate housing conveniently located within just a block away from the medical school and NYU Langone Hospital-Long Island.  Apartment-style units including studio, small and large one-bedroom, and two-bedroom shared options is guaranteed to all single students when they first matriculate.  Housing for couples and families may be available.  Smoking and pets are not permitted. 

For more information:  
https://medli.nyu.edu/students/housing
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: NYUGLISOM is committed to providing equal educational opportunity and participation for students with disabilities. To inquire about academic accommodations, disability-related accessible housing, or other accessibility services, please contact the New York University Moses Center for Accessibility and Inclusive Culture:   mosescenter@nyu.edu or visit their website (https://www.nyu.edu/life/community-flourishing/centers-and-communities/accessibility.html).
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
An accelerated three-year program can be challenging even for the most capable and well-adapted student.  As such, student mental health and well-being is a top priority at NYUGLISOM and a myriad of wellness programs, individual support and medical care resources are available to insure students' mental, emotional and physical well-being.  

For more information:
https://medli.nyu.edu/education/md-degree/md-student-resources/health-services
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Our small class size (24 per class) fosters an unusually close-knit student community united by a common purpose grounded in primary care and humanism in a learning environment that fosters teamwork, collaboration and collegiality & where each student's unique contributions are highly valued.  

We are also committed to supporting students' professional growth & pair our pioneering educational program with a comprehensive career and academic advising program that incorporates a combination of highly individualized academic coaching, residency advising, and role-matched mentoring.  Our students are further supported by our easily accessible teaching and clinical faculty & academic leaders who enthusiastically serve as inspiring educators, role-models, research mentors, advisors and future colleagues.

We equally prioritize our students' personal well-being and growth through our robust health and wellness programming to ensure they remain grounded and fulfilled during medical school.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Academic learning takes place on campus at the NYUGLISOM Research & Academic Center.  Clinical training primarily takes places directly across the street from the school at NYU Langone Hospital-Long Island.  Some clinical training also takes place at NYU Langone Hospital-Suffolk.  Ambulatory clinical experiences take place in community-based outpatient physician practices in Nassau & Suffolk counties.  Students will need a car to travel to most of these required off-campus clinical placements.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Our innovative. three-year accelerated program produces exemplary primary care physicians who are exceptionally trained and empowered to become leaders in the delivery of comprehensive, continuous, coordinated, collaborative, culturally-competent, patient-centered and community-based care AND who are committed to pursue residency training and future professional practice as general practitioners the primary care disciplines of internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics & gynecology or general surgery.   Our program also supports students interested in pursuing residency training in family medicine and has an established track record of graduates' externally matching at top-tier family medicine graduate training programs.

NYUGLISOM 's highly integrated, problem-based curriculum is specifically designed to foster a lifelong active learning mindset that will enable our students to effectively and efficiently study the medical sciences and acquire the highest clinical proficiency that underpins a comprehensive medical education while simultaneously gaining specific expertise in the principles of primary care and a mastery in health systems science—the study of how healthcare is delivered, how healthcare providers work together and strategies to deliver high quality, value-based, equitable patient care. 
   
More detailed information about our transformative curriculum is available on our website:  https://medli.nyu.edu/curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
The principles of primary care form the core of our medical education program.  

The first-year Practice of Medicine course integrates foundational clinical skills and early patient-contact with the practice of primary care medicine.  

The three-year Continuity Ambulatory Practice Experience is a sequence of ambulatory experiences in primary care disciplines of internal medicine, family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, geriatrics, and general surgery.  

The second-year required Primary Care clerkship at affiliated ambulatory sites provides students training in management of common primary care complaints, chronic conditions and preventative care.  Hospice care and physical rehabilitation are also part of this clerkship experience. 

Final-year electives provide additional time for primary care-focused training and/or research.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Students are encouraged to pursue extra-curricular research during their medical education that span translational, clinical, population/community health, health systems science, and quality assurance.  Due to the accelerated curriculum, there are limited opportunities for students to engage in extended basic science research.  Biannual student research workshops are offered to allow students to interact with potential faculty mentors and initiate research collaborations. Students also have access a catalogue of existing faculty and resident research projects across many departments and divisions that are seeking research assistance and are also encouraged to independently seek out NYUGLISOM faculty for research opportunities who are eager to support students' particular interests.

For more information about NYUGLISOM research:

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
NYUGLISOM's primary-care focused mission incorporates an innovative, three-year accelerated curriculum and a directed-pathway to residency option at NYU Langone Hospital–Long Island in the fields of internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics & gynecology or general surgery.  Students interested in family medicine are also encouraged to apply and are supported by the school to successfully match externally to top-tier family medicine residency programs. 

Three-year Full-Tuition Scholarships are awarded to all students regardless of financial need or merit and need-based Debt-Free Scholarships to students who financially qualify - to help pay for costs of attendance above tuition - enabling NYUGLISOM students to graduate unencumbered by excessive student debt. 

Located 17 miles east of New York City, the school is adjacent to our teaching hospital and campus housing in the suburban Village of Mineola in Nassau County-Long Island & easily accessible to shops, restaurants and recreation.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
MISSION
NYU Grossman Long Island School of Medicine's mission is to develop preeminent physician leaders through scholarship and innovative medical education design anchored in the principles of primary care and health systems science.  

VISION
Our vision is to improve the health of the communities we serve by advancing medical education, scientific discovery, and comprehensive, equitable, collaborative health care delivery.

                                                                                                                    * * * * * * * * 
NYU Grossman Long Island School of Medicine (NYUGLISOM) is one of two distinct medical schools under the nationally ranked NYU Langone Health System banner affiliated with New York University (NYU).  NYUGLISOM's specific mission is to address the growing physician workforce shortage of general practitioners in primary care fields and empower our graduates to become leaders in the delivery of high-quality, value-based, coordinated, and equitable healthcare that is patient-focused, family-centered and community-based.   

Our pioneering, three-year, accelerated undergraduate medical education program combines innovations in medical education together with exceptional clinical training that is anchored in the principles of primary care and health systems science.  By streamlining entry into clinical practice by one full year, we enable our graduates to impact the health of the community as quickly as possible.   

Further, we are the only medical school in the country that specifically pairs students' acceptance to medical school with the offer of a directed-pathway to residency in specific primary care fields including:  internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics & gynecology and general surgery.   This residency directed pathway option is linked to our teaching hospital, NYU Langone Hospital - Long Island.   

A career path in family medicine also aligns with the school's primary care mission.  Students interested in family medicine enter NYU GLISOM via the internal medicine track and are fully supported by the school to successfully match to an external family medicine program.

Three-year Full-Tuition Scholarships are awarded to all students regardless of financial need or merit and additional need-based Debt-Free Scholarships are offered to students who financially qualify - to help pay for costs of attendance above tuition - enabling NYU GLISOM students to graduate unencumbered by excessive student debt. 

Our comprehensive admissions review process directly aligns with our primary care mission and three-year, accelerated educational program that offers of a directed pathway to residency at the time of admission.   We seek exceptionally qualified candidates who demonstrate (1) a clear commitment to the principles of primary care and (2) significant experience in the field of medicine associated with their selected residency track or family medicine. 

To best prepare our graduates to become critical thinkers and life-long learners, NYU GLISOM’s curriculum has a strong emphasis on ‘active learning’ that incorporates a problem-based, small-group, collaborative approach. Unparalleled longitudinal support, advising, and mentoring is also an integral part of the program to insure students' success and well-being in all aspects of their medical school journey.  Additionally, the small-size of our program fosters a unique sense of community and camaraderie among students, faculty and senior leaders which directly aligns with the team-based mindset that personifies a primary care physician.  

Though we are a small school, we seek to make a big impact and the entire NYUGLISOM community takes great pride in the success of our graduates who serve as exemplars of our primary care mission and vision - many of whom have become leaders in their residency programs, continue to be engaged in impactful scholarly research, and selflessly give back to the communities they now serve.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
We accept a pre-health advisor or committee composite letter and/or letter packets from your undergraduate or graduate program in fulfillment of our letter requirements.  You may also choose to submit additional individual letters in addition to a pre-health advisor or committee composite letter.  If you are only submitting individual letters, a minimum of three letters of evaluation is required, and at least two of these letters should be from science professors.  Letters from MD supervisors are strongly encouraged, if applicable.

Best letters usually come from individuals who know you well such as current/former professors,  physician mentors, research or employer supervisors.   All individual letters must be on official letterhead and submitted through the AMCAS Letter Service unless otherwise instructed by your undergraduate or graduate program that is preparing a letter packet on your behalf.  

For more specific information please email: medli.admissions@nyulangone.org.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
The goals of the NYUGLISOM interview program are two-fold:

-To learn more about applicants' commitment to primary care and their selected residency track along with their personal attributes and interpersonal, communication, and teamwork skills utilizing the MMI format and an interactive team-based group activity.  

-To provide applicants an opportunity to learn more about our medical education program directly from our academic leaders, faculty, and students.

Details about the interview day as well as informational video presentations are sent to applicants approximately one week prior to their interview date. Also included are links to a live orientation conducted by the associate dean for admission and a separate, informal 'meet & greet' session hosted by our current students.  This orientation takes place on Monday @ 5p(ET) of the week of an applicant's scheduled interview.

For more information:

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
PRIMARY/SECONDARY SUBMISSION DEADLINES
Our primary AMCAS application submission deadline is November 2nd  and our school-specific secondary application deadline is November 15th @ 11:59pm ET.  To facilitate timely review, applicants are strongly encouraged to complete and submit both applications as early as possible.

COURSEWORK/GRADES
We will accept pass/fail grades for coursework (including labs) pursuant to the COVID grading policies that were in effect at the undergraduate or graduate institution(s) where these courses were completed.   Online courses taken during these specific semesters will also be accepted.   We understand applicants may have concerns about the impact of pass/fail grades during COVID may have had on their GPA.  The admissions committee takes this into account when conducting its assessment of a candidate’s academic readiness to succeed in our accelerated three-year curriculum.

INTERVIEWS
Virtual interviews are conducted September through mid-December.  Applications are continuously reviewed throughout the interview season and applicants may be invited for an interview at any time during this period.  

POST INTERVIEW STATUS
Interviewed applicants can expect to be notified approximately 4-6 weeks after their interview date with one of three outcomes:
1.  Advanced to final pool for acceptance consideration
2.  Application has been placed 'on hold' and may be reviewed again later in the application cycle
3.  Candidate is no longer considered for a spot in the entering class

ADMISSION DECISIONS
NYU GLISOM is committed to giving every candidate in the final pool full consideration for acceptance.  Therefore, we do not offer rolling admissions.  Initial acceptance offers are made on a single notification date in mid-February via personal phone call from a member of the admissions committee.  All other final pool candidates are notified on this date via email if they have been placed on our waitlist or no longer considered for a spot in the entering class.

We only maintain 24 accepted students at one time.  Applicants are accepted off the waitlist should a spot associated with their selected residency track become available.  To help manage expectations, waitlisted applicants are notified as soon as all accepted candidates in a specific residency track have committed to enroll (CTE) to NYU GLISOM and no additional acceptances for that track are expected. 

FOR MORE DETAILED INFORMATION:
https://medli.nyu.edu/education/md-degree/md-admissions
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
MCAT scores are among the metrics used to assess the academic readiness of applicants for success in our rigorous, three-year accelerated program.  If multiple MCAT scores are submitted, emphasis is placed on the most recent score which is considered to be representative of the applicant's most current foundational knowledge, critical thinking and analytical skills.  

We only consider MCAT scores from three years prior to your expected matriculation date.  For example, if you plan to enroll in July 2027, the oldest acceptable MCAT score will be from January 2024.  Further, September 12, 2026 is the latest MCAT test administration date for your score to be released to meet our November 16th 2026 application completion deadline.  In fairness to all applicants, there are no exceptions to these deadlines.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo:
Though we do not have a minimum MCAT threshold for screening, significant emphasis is placed on evidence of an applicant's foundational knowledge, critical thinking and analytical skills assessed by the MCAT and is incorporated into our comprehensive review process.  

Please see section on 'Acceptance Data' for additional information about MCAT scores of our accepted and matriculated students.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo:
Both an applicant's TOTAL & SCIENCE GPA's are among the metrics used to assess their readiness to handle the rigor and pace of the pre-clinical phase of our accelerated medical education curriculum.   

Evidence of exceptional and sustained academic success in science coursework, along with demonstrated intellectual engagement in declared major/minor coursework is a key element of our comprehensive review of a candidate's readiness to be successful in our active, self-directed learning environment.  

NYUGLISOM does not have required premedical coursework.  However, applicants are expected to demonstrate exemplary preparation in the sciences. Science coursework taken more than 3 years prior to application is accepted but may raise concerns about an applicant's current foundational knowledge base and ability to handle the academic demands of our accelerated curriculum.

Please see section on 'Acceptance Data' for additional GPA information on our accepted and matriculated students
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo:
We recognize an applicant's undergraduate performance may not be fully representative of their academic potential.  Additional consideration is given to other factors that may have impacted a candidate's academic performance  in undergrad (i.e.) financial need for paid employment that may have taken time away from academic work or navigating significant obstacles during college.   

If applicable, applicants who initially may not have performed up to their potential during undergrad are expected to demonstrate consistent and exceptional academic performance during any subsequent undergraduate post-bac or master's program coursework. 

Please see section on 'Acceptance Data' for additional GPA information on our accepted and matriculated students
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo:
We do not have a minimum number of credit hours in order to consider an applicant's postbac or graduate coursework.  

Evidence of consistent exceptional academic success while completing a rigorous course load over successive semesters and at the same time managing competing priorities  (e.g.) paid employment, extensive research, community service or other volunteer activities or navigating extenuating family obligations, is incorporated into our comprehensive review of a candidate's ability to handle the demands of our accelerated three-year curriculum.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: NYUGLISOM does not have specific pre-medical course requirements.  However, applicants' demonstrated academic achievement in introductory and upper level science coursework is a significant factor in assessing their academic readiness for successfully navigating the rigor and pace of our three-year accelerated curriculum.  We recognize that students may begin their undergraduate studies at a community college and the committee on admissions will consider candidates' performance in introductory coursework completed at these undergraduate programs.  However, evidence of competence in upper level science coursework completed at a four-year institution is also expected.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Interview thank you notes, letters of continued interest  or  intent to matriculate as well as notification of significant updates or achievements are accepted and should be directly uploaded to your portal on the NYUGLISOM admissions platform.  This is the most reliable process to insure the admissions committee will read this updated information as part of it's ongoing review of your application.  Please do not submit these updates to the NYU GLISOM admissions general email inbox.  Unfortunately, due to the volume of updates we receive, we are unable to respond to email requests to confirm receipt.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
NYU GLISOM will consider for admission any applicant who meets its academic and non-academic criteria and who demonstrates the ability to perform the skills listed our Technical Standards, with or without reasonable accommodations, consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Rehabilitation Act.

NYU GLISOM provides reasonable accommodations for all qualified individuals with disabilities who apply for admission to the MD degree program and who are enrolled as medical students. Otherwise qualified individuals will not be excluded from admission or participation in the NYUGLISOM's educational programs and activities based solely on their status as a person with a disability. 

It is the responsibility of a candidate with a disability, or a candidate who develops a disability, who requires accommodations to meet these technical standards to self-disclose to the Associate Dean for Admissions at: medli.admissions@nyulangone.org.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
NYU Grossman Long Island School of Medicine is proud to award three-year Full-Tuition Scholarships to all matriculated students regardless of merit or financial need  provided they maintain academic progress and professionalism standards.   

Additional need-based Debt-Free Scholarships are available to students who financially qualify (based on school-specific verification requirements) to help pay for costs of attendance beyond tuition - enabling our graduates to complete medical school unencumbered by significant student debt and is dramatically lower than the average medical student debt nationally. 

We also fully subsidize the cost of individual NYU Grossman Long Island School of Medicine Student Health Insurance for all three years for all matriculated students.

As well, our office of financial aid offers a robust financial literacy program to assist our students to maximize their financial well-being while in medical school and beyond.  In addition, we provide individualized debt-management counseling for those students who may utilize loans while in medical school.

The 2026-27 NYUGLISOM estimated cost of attendance is available on the school's website:
https://medli.nyu.edu/education/md-degree/financial-aid/cost-attendance

medSchoolPrograms.info: Due to the highly integrated format of our three-year accelerated curriculum, NYU GLISOM does not offer combined or dual degree programs.  Additionally,  our mission is to streamline students' entry into primary care.  Thus we are unable to grant requests for a year (or more) leave of absence to complete a combined or dual degree at another institution.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: PLAN TO ENROLL:  Applicants who plan to enroll to NYUGLISOM are strongly encouraged select this option as soon as possible after of this date.

NARROW ACCEPTANCE OFFERS:  Applicants are strongly encouraged to narrow their acceptances to no more than three schools by this date and withdraw from any other additional schools where they are holding acceptances.

COMMIT TO ENROLL:  Applicants who are committed to attending NYUGLISOM are strongly urged to utilize this option as soon as it becomes available and are expected to withdraw from all schools where they are holding an acceptance or waitlist spot.  Applicants who commit to enroll at another medical school will be automatically withdrawn from our applicant pool roster.

NYUGLISOM FINAL COMMIT TO ENROLL DEADLINE:   Applicants MUST commit to enroll by 12-noon EST on this date and have withdrawn from all schools where they are holding an acceptance or waitlist spot in order to secure their spot in the incoming class. Failure to comply will result in withdrawal with the applicant's NYUGLISOM acceptance.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The admissions committee seeks applicants who not only excel academically but who also exhibit intellectual curiosity as evidenced by the breadth and depth of their coursework.  We encourage students majoring in any field of study, including the humanities and social sciences to apply, and particularly value applicants who demonstrate a passion for their academic area of interest.  

While we do not mandate prerequisite coursework, applicants are expected to demonstrate proficiency in biology, chemistry, physics, genetics, statistics, English, psychology, and sociology.   In addition, the admissions committee closely evaluates the academic readiness of each applicant in the context of the unique demands of the accelerated pace of our curriculum.  

Evidence of exemplary readiness in the AAMC Core Competencies for Entering Medical Students as well as applicants' individual background and unique life experiences are also highly valued.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: While we do not have specific course requirements, relevant science coursework should be taken within 3 years of matriculation to ensure entering students' strong foundational scientific knowledge.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
We utilize a comprehensive review process that incorporates an individualized, balanced assessment of applicants’ experiences, attributes and metrics to identify those who best align with our school's primary care mission, directed pathway to residency option and accelerated educational curriculum.  Further, we value applicants who embody an ethos of service and a commitment to improving the human condition steeped in respect, humility, empathy and compassion.  Applicants who have previously pursued a career in other areas of clinical care or taken a non-traditional path towards medicine are encouraged to apply.  

Strongest applicants reflect:
- A commitment to pursue a generalist career focused on primary care principles
- Experiences and insights that directly align with their selected residency pathway or family medicine.
- Academic, professional and personal readiness to handle the demands of a rigorous, accelerated program
- Ties to the broader communities served by the school
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText:
NYUGLISOM views shadowing as an introductory experience for prospective applicants to learn more broadly about medicine, clinical practice and the patient-doctor relationship.  

Applicants who best align with our school's mission are those who have extensive primary-care focused experiences that speak to their understanding of comprehensive, continuous, longitudinal culturally-sensitive health care. 

Since NYUGLISOM also pairs acceptance with the offer of a directed pathway to specific primary care residencies in fields of internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics & gynecology or general surgery,  it is expected that applicants possess in-depth confirmatory experiences that demonstrate a clear understanding and commitment to practicing as a generalist in their selected residency track OR as a family medicine practitioner.

Applicants interested in a subspecialty or a physician-scientist career path are not the best fit for our school's generalist primary care mission.
